editorial.meta_description: The FRM Part 1 - Financial Risk Manager exam from GARP assesses risk management, quantitative analysis, financial markets, and valuation models.
editorial.overview: The FRM Part 1 - Financial Risk Manager exam is administered by GARP. It assesses knowledge across four domains: Foundations of Risk Management, Quantitative Analysis, Financial Markets and Products, and Valuation and Risk Models. This 240-minute exam consists of 100 questions, providing a standardized assessment of the technical skills needed to manage financial risk in professional settings. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in these four core areas to earn the designation, ensuring they possess the necessary expertise to navigate complex financial environments and mitigate risks effectively.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is intended for individuals pursuing the Financial Risk Manager certification. It is suitable for professionals seeking to demonstrate their technical knowledge of risk management, quantitative methods, and financial product valuation within the global financial industry.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official FRM Learning Objectives and the FRM Study Guide provided by GARP. Focus on the four domains, which carry weights of 20%, 20%, 30%, and 30% respectively. Use the provided syllabus to guide your self-study, ensuring you understand the specific readings and learning objectives for each area. Practice applying these concepts to the types of questions found on the 100-question exam to ensure you are prepared for the testing environment.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers the basic principles and concepts of risk management. It provides the framework for understanding how various risks are identified, measured, and managed within modern financial institutions and professional organizations to ensure stability.

This domain focuses on the mathematical and statistical tools required for risk analysis. It covers the quantitative methods used to measure and model various types of financial risk in practice for professional applications and analysis.

This domain examines the structure and function of financial markets and the characteristics of various financial products. It represents a significant portion of the exam weight and requires a deep technical understanding of market operations.

This domain covers the models used for the valuation of financial instruments and the assessment of risk. It focuses on the application of these models in real-world financial risk scenarios for professional practitioners and analysts.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive prepared for a 240-minute session containing 100 questions. Manage your time effectively across the four domains to ensure you address all sections within the allotted duration and maximize your potential for success on the exam.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The FRM Part 1 - Financial Risk Manager exam consists of 100 questions in total. Candidates should be prepared to answer all of these within the allotted time frame to demonstrate their technical proficiency.
The exam follows a pass/fail scoring system. GARP does not publish a specific numerical passing score, so candidates should aim to master all domains to ensure success on the certification exam.
The exam has a duration of 240 minutes. This time is intended to cover all 100 questions, so effective time management is necessary for all candidates taking the test to complete the sections.

faq.question_title: Where can I find the current certification path?
faq.answer_text: For information regarding the long-term certification path or any updates to the program, please check with GARP directly to ensure you have the most accurate and current information for your career.
